children: The cement maker has deployed more than 70 electric vehicles and achieved nearly 100 per cent EV-based clinker dispatches on its Sirohi–Kalol route
JK Lakshmi Cement plans to expand its electric vehicle (EV) fleet to 120 vehicles by March 2027, as it increases the use of electric trucks for transporting clinker across Rajasthan and Gujarat.

The company has already deployed more than 70 electric vehicles across routes connecting its Sirohi plant in Rajasthan with its Kalol grinding unit, Palanpur unit and Surat grinding unit. It has also achieved nearly 100 per cent EV-based clinker dispatches on the Sirohi–Kalol route.
JK Lakshmi Cement is working with electric vehicle logistics providers SwitchLabs and Billion E to support the deployment across its transportation network.
Electric Trucks Expand Across Logistics Routes
The Sirohi–Kalol route marks a key step in the company's use of electric vehicles for long-distance freight transportation in the cement industry.
The company plans to build on its existing fleet as it expands electric vehicle deployment across other routes.
Vinita Singhania, Chairperson and Managing Director of JK Lakshmi Cement, said the company was integrating sustainable practices across its operations while focusing on long-term business efficiency.
She said the shift to electric vehicle-based clinker dispatches between Sirohi and Kalol was an important milestone in the company's efforts to scale cleaner transportation.
The electric vehicle programme forms part of JK Lakshmi Cement's broader decarbonisation strategy, which aims to reduce emissions across its value chain.
The company said it is pursuing sustainability initiatives to improve operational efficiency and support its long-term ambition of achieving net-zero emissions by 2047.

The fleet expansion comes as industrial companies explore electric vehicles to reduce the environmental impact of freight transportation. For cement manufacturers, logistics is an important area of focus because moving raw materials and finished products requires substantial transportation.
